text: This is NodeRoom — a shared workspace where people and A.I. agents edit the same spreadsheets, and every agent edit stays reviewable. The demo on the right is running live: the room agent commits variance numbers, and each one carries a citation back to its source.

Creating a room asks one question before anything else: how should agent edits land? The recommended default is review — every artifact change waits for your approval. Auto-approve is available, and even then, every write remains traced.
Joining is just as light. A room shares a code, not a seat.
And the sample room is honest about itself — it tells you its data is synthetic, not live research.
The landing can also prove its claims. These drills run the very same engine calls as a live room.
First, a stale write. The engine rejects it and returns the conflict as data. Nothing is overwritten.
When an agent loses a race to a human, its draft does not silently merge. It becomes a review proposal.
A person approves, and the change re-applies at the current version — not the stale baseline. Reviewed, then applied. That is the whole product.
